Browser version: texture swizzling on a helper thread, per-thread load in diagnostics (#10)

* Browser version: texture swizzling on a helper thread, per-thread load in diagnostics

A phone diagnostic showed the VIF1/VU1 worker at 89-97% busy (the game thread
75-80%, GL thread ~5 ms/frame). Transfer swizzling moves from that worker to a
helper thread; the GS thread waits for a transfer's blocks when it reaches it,
so the original order is kept. The 5 s statistics now report the VU1 worker's
and the game thread's load.

Terrain contour lines: stop the flicker with jitter on (#18)

* Terrain contour lines: give them an un-jittered depth

The terrain tool's contour lines are drawn by the terrain shader from a copy of
last frame's depth (colorMapDepthTex), rebuilt with the game's un-jittered
camera. With jitter on, that depth is shifted by last frame's jitter, so the
lines jump every frame. The motion-vector pass now also writes the depth with
the jitter taken out, and while a pipeline that reads colorMapDepthTex is bound
in the scene pass the layer binds a copy of its set pointing at that image.

Don't let one hung game stop the other windows' triggers

PrintWindow waits for a window's program to draw it, so while one watched
game was "Not Responding" every check sat in PrintWindow for as long as it
hung, and the other games' pictures never fired. A window that doesn't
answer at once (IsHungAppWindow, or a 50 ms WM_NULL) isn't copied that
check, and isn't counted as one that can't be seen.

UnknownTextureFormatChoice reads it: manager, groups 0, the render
target's pixel format as the opaque format, 0x115c (4444) as the alpha
format and 0 halvings. KrustyUI's copy sets +0x14 to 1 when video memory
is short. +0x20..+0x30 become textureOpaqueGroup, textureAlphaGroup,
textureOpaqueFormat, textureAlphaFormat and textureHalvings; the copy's
fields take UnknownTextureFormatChoic

DXGI and D3D9 present events only cover Direct3D. Every present also ends in
the Windows graphics kernel, which emits DxgKrnl Present_Info (id 184) once per
swap, attributed to the app. That is now a third frame source: the API-level
count is preferred, and the kernel count wins when it is well above it (a
Vulkan or OpenGL game with a small DXGI overlay window). Verified with an
OpenGL test program (189 fps measured). --probe --raw <pid> counts one process's
events separately, for checking new APIs.

raises. The hung child

GPU: readback commands run in order on the draw recording thread (#180)

Game threads ask the GPU thread for readbacks (deferred readback, download, texture readback
wait) through SendCommand; the GPU thread drained the whole draw pipe before running any of
them: 20-40 drains/s that cost 5-22% of its time in the city (TLG_DCB_STATS "commands"). These
commands only need to run after the draws handed over before them, which is what RunInOrder
gives: they go into the pipe as ordered tasks and the GPU thread keeps decoding. Flips and
anything else still drain. Live switch: TlgToggle::PipelinedComm

Draw pipe: a drain that outlives its spin sleeps on CPUs with few threads (#177)

The GPU command thread waited for the draw recording thread with 4096 pauses and then
sched_yield for the rest of the wait: ~8% of all CPU samples on a 16-thread machine, where it
costs nothing, but a whole core taken from the game's threads on CPUs with 4-6 cores. With
fewer than 12 hardware threads (TLG_DRAIN_SLEEP=0/1 overrides) the drain now waits on
`consumed` (futex) after the spin; stage B notifies after each advance while a waiter is
counted, so no wake-up is lost.

the one adjustment the game can make to a mark without pricing anything.
